series.title: Sherlock Holmes: The Baker Street Casebook
series.logline: A wounded army doctor answers an advertisement for lodgings and walks into the most amazing adventure of his life.
series.summary: Doctor John Watson returns wounded from Afghanistan, meets an eccentric chemist named Sherlock Holmes, and takes rooms with him at two two one B, Baker Street. Across two cases, a poisoned inheritance and a diplomat's murdered visitor, Watson learns that the difference between success and disaster is always the little things.
series.narrator: Doctor John Watson, first person, retrospective

critical_constraints: Gemini multi-speaker config supports a MAXIMUM OF 2 speakers per call. Scenes here often have 3 or more. Synthesise line by line with single-speaker calls and stitch with pydub.
The lines[] array is the single source of truth. Never hand raw JSON to the TTS model.
Every text value is already TTS-safe: no asterisks, hashes, underscores, brackets, em dashes, ellipses, or markdown of any kind.
Abbreviations are expanded in full: Doctor not Dr, Mister not Mr, Missus not Mrs, Inspector not Insp.
Numbers are spelled out as they should be spoken: two two one B, thirty eight calibre, three hundred pounds.
Do not send stage directions to the TTS model. Use the style_prompt field instead.
tts.global_style_prompt: Read as a nineteen fifties radio detective drama. Measured pace, clear diction, understated British delivery. Let pauses carry tension. Never rush a deduction.

NARRATOR.note: Watson looking back. Warm, unhurried, slightly wry.

WATSON.note: Same voice as narrator. Watson is the narrator.

HOLMES.note: Crisp, quick, faintly amused. Speeds up on deductions.

LORD_BERYL.note: Clipped, senior, used to being obeyed.

ROSS.note: Helpful, precise, one shade too helpful.

tts.voice_names_warning: Gemini prebuilt voice names change between model versions. Verify against the current API before batch rendering. Fall back to edge-tts if a name is rejected.

style_guide.tone: Dry, warm, faintly astonished. The comedy comes from Watson being one step behind.
style_guide.pacing: Deductions land fast. Everything around them is unhurried.
style_guide.narrative_voice: Plain declarative sentences. Watson never oversells Holmes, which is what makes Holmes land.
dialogue_rules: Holmes answers a question with a better question, or with the answer three steps ahead.
Watson asks what the listener is thinking.
Lestrade is never stupid, only certain.
Nobody explains a deduction until Holmes chooses to.
forbidden: Holmes being cruel to Watson. He is impatient, never contemptuous.
Onscreen gore. Violence is reported, not described.
Any deduction the listener could not have made from something already stated.

characters.name: Sherlock Holmes
characters.description: A consulting chemist and the first man to devise a reliable test for bloodstains.
characters.personality: Brilliant, restless, indifferent to credit and to any fact he judges useless.
characters.backstory: Working on forensic chemistry at Bart's when Watson meets him. Beats corpses with a stick to study post mortem bruising.
characters.goals: Establish criminal investigation as a science.
characters.flaw: He discards knowledge he deems irrelevant, including that the Earth circles the Sun.
characters.speech_style: Rapid, precise, faintly amused. Asks a question he already knows the answer to.
knows: Sensational literature and every major crime of the last hundred years
characters.signature_line: It is the little things that make the difference between success and disaster.

characters.name: Doctor John Watson
characters.description: An army doctor invalided home from Afghanistan.
characters.personality: Decent, observant by training, repeatedly astonished.
characters.backstory: Wounded in the shoulder in Afghanistan, contracted a tropical fever, discharged with instructions to rest.
characters.goals: Find comfortable quarters at a reasonable price. Then, keep up.
characters.flaw: He sees everything Holmes sees and concludes nothing from it.
characters.speech_style: Plain, courteous, asks the obvious question on the listener's behalf.
characters.narrative_function: The listener's proxy. Every explanation in the series is delivered to him.

characters.name: Inspector Lestrade
characters.description: Scotland Yard. Competent, conventional, and always one certainty ahead of the evidence.
characters.personality: Proud, decent, defensive. Takes the credit and means no harm by it.
characters.goals: Close the case cleanly and quickly.
characters.flaw: He decides what happened and then collects the facts that agree.
characters.speech_style: Official, blunt. Repeats his position louder when challenged.
characters.spin_off_note: SECONDARY SPIN-OFF CANDIDATE. Recurring across both cases, consistently wrong in an interesting way, and the only character with an ongoing relationship to Holmes that changes.

characters.name: Stamford
characters.description: An old acquaintance of Watson's who makes the introduction.

characters.name: Peter Cunningham
characters.description: A wealthy man, secretly married a week before his death. Stabbed in his own home.
characters.note: Dead before the case opens. Appears only in testimony.

characters.name: Missus Cunningham
characters.description: Peter's secret wife. Served nine months in Holloway five years ago for theft.
characters.note: The transcript never gives her a first name. None has been invented.

characters.name: Ralph Cunningham
characters.motive: Peter was buying up his promissory notes and had given him one week to leave the country.

characters.name: Missus Cunningham senior
characters.description: Peter's mother. Certain the widow murdered her son.

characters.name: Lord Beryl
characters.description: Senior official of the Foreign Office.
characters.personality: Correct, protective of his wife, unaware of his own household.

characters.name: Lady Beryl
characters.description: Austrian born, raised in America, five years in England.
characters.personality: Composed under arrest. Lies well and for good reasons.
characters.secret: Confessed to a murder she did not commit, believing she was shielding her husband.

characters.name: Herr Oberstein
characters.description: Austrian freelance agent who bought and sold anything he could get his hands on.
characters.note: Killed by a blow to the head, not by the revolver found beside him.

characters.name: Mister Ross
characters.personality: Impeccably helpful. Volunteers one correction too many.
characters.motive: Selling Foreign Office secrets to Oberstein, then killing him to keep the money and the papers.

characters.name: Sergeant Wilkins
characters.description: A retired sergeant of Marines, now a police messenger.

relationships.evolves: Ep 1 strangers, Ep 3 flatmates, Ep 6 partners, Ep 12 settled friendship
Ep 5 open conflict, Ep 6 Lestrade takes the credit, Ep 7 Lestrade defends Holmes to the press, Ep 12 asks for him by name

relationships.note: Lestrade likes Watson because Watson agrees with him.
Stamford makes the introduction and vanishes from the series.
Married a week, at Brighton. Concealed at Peter's request.
Each believes they are protecting the other.

objects.name: The bloodstain test
objects.significance: Holmes's haemoglobin precipitation test. The reason Watson takes him seriously.

objects.name: Two two one B, Baker Street
objects.significance: The rooms. Taken in episode two, occupied from episode three.

objects.name: The violin
objects.significance: Holmes asks whether Watson minds it before he asks anything else.

objects.name: The anchor tattoo
objects.significance: On the back of the messenger's hand. How Holmes knows he is a retired Marine.

objects.name: The knife
objects.significance: In Peter Cunningham's chest. The widow pulled it out, which is what damned her.

objects.name: The chequebook
objects.significance: A thousand pounds drawn every week for six weeks. Peter buying up Ralph's promissory notes.

objects.name: The marks on the carpet
objects.significance: Signs of a struggle. Peter was over six feet. He would not have lost to the woman accused.

objects.name: The sunburn and the ring mark
objects.significance: Fading sunburn, a new ring indentation, on both their hands. A weekend at Brighton. They were married.

objects.name: The pygmy poison extract
objects.significance: Holmes's running experiment. He leaves the gas on under it. The last line of the series.

objects.name: Oberstein's revolver
objects.significance: A Schmidt thirty eight found beside the body. Never fired. Lady Beryl saw it and assumed.

objects.name: The broken eyeglasses
objects.significance: Oberstein put them on to read the papers he was buying. They broke when he fell. Ross gathered up the pieces and threw the frames into the garden.

world_rules.description: Every conclusion must rest on something physically present and already mentioned to the listener.

world_rules.rule: The police are certain, not stupid
world_rules.description: Lestrade's errors always come from deciding first and looking second.
The listener never learns anything before Watson does, except what they can see for themselves.

plot_threads.summary: Holmes's forensic research and his campaign for scientific investigation.
The murder of Herr Oberstein and who sold the Foreign Office secrets.
Why Lady Beryl confessed to a murder she did not commit.
